title: Beatrix and the Signal
premise: Tamsin Joubert is the last active terraformer on Meridian Reach, tending a garden engineered for colonists still frozen in orbit — a colony split between two cryo-ships whose crews stopped speaking to each other generations ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she discovers the ships' silence was manufactured: one faction sabotaged the other's life support to claim the single jump window out of a dying system. As the window closes, Tamsin must choose which ship's sleepers to wake and carry through, knowing the other half will drift forever. She wakes both, splitting her garden's resources to keep half of each crew alive, and jumps alone into the dark carrying the truth that reunites what betrayal divided.
about_author: C. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years working remote environmental monitoring stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet, plant-forward science fiction about people who maintain things no one remembers to thank them for.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She runs her supply circuit between the derelict terraforming stations and the silent cryo-ships Halcyon and Vesper, talking to the sleeping colonists over open comms because no one else answers. Establishes her loneliness, her devotion to the unborn garden, and the strange ritual of speaking to two ships that never speak back. Emotional beat: tender isolation.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The distress signal arrives in Old Meridian Standard, dead for two centuries, broadcast from Vesper itself. Decoding it with an archive AI, she finds a plea for help dated forty years ago — sent repeatedly, never answered. Someone aboard has been awake all along. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath wonder.

chapters.title: The Man in the Cold
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Ede Okonkwo, awake for four decades inside Vesper, has kept the sleepers alive by cannibalizing his own future. He reveals the sabotage: Halcyon's crew cut Vesper's power during the original crisis, choosing their own survival. Ede answered with silence and a slow plan. Emotional beat: righteous fury curdled into patience.

chapters.title: What the Garden Was For
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She cross-checks Ede's claims against station logs and finds corroborating evidence — but also evidence he has edited some records himself. Her loyalty to the mission, and to the idea that she serves everyone equally, fractures. She visits Halcyon's hull and finds scorch marks from the old attack. Emotional beat: disillusionment.

chapters.title: Two Ships, One Window
chapters.summary: Ede's POV. The jump window opens in ninety days; only one ship can be prepped in time. Ede asks Tamsin to wake Vesper's sleepers and abandon Halcyon as justice. Flashbacks show the night of the sabotage from his side — including a detail he omits: Vesper fired first. Emotional beat: sympathy built on a lie.

chapters.title: The Archive's Confession
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The archive AI, reconstructing corrupted logs, surfaces the full truth: both crews attacked each other within the same hour, each believing they were retaliating first. The silence between the ships was mutual shame, not villainy. Tamsin realizes Ede has spent forty years avenging a crime that was really a tragedy. Emotional beat: grief for a war nobody won.

chapters.title: Ninety Days of Light
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tamsin confronts Ede; he breaks, admitting he let the false version stand because the truth gave him nothing to live for. Together they attempt the impossible: prep both ships by diverting the garden's growth systems, spending the terraforming project itself as fuel. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership, shared sacrifice.

chapters.title: Halcyon Wakes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Waking Halcyon's sleepers first, she faces their captain, Suri Anand, who learns what her ancestors did — and what was done to them. Some crew refuse to share a jump with Vesper's survivors. Tamsin must argue for mercy to people who have every reason to withhold it. Emotional beat: moral courage against inherited hatred.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Ede's POV, climax. Systems fail under the doubled load; the window begins closing with half of each crew still unfrozen. Ede chooses to stay behind manually holding Vesper's core together, trading his life for the launch. Tamsin refuses to leave him and instead jettisons the garden's seed vault — her life's work — to buy the seconds. Emotional beat: devastating choice, love expressed as loss.

chapters.title: Beatrix Blooms
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, resolution. Aboard the merged fleet-ship Beatrix, the woken halves of humanity grieve and begin again, carrying Ede's name and the true history Tamsin transmits to every bunk. In the hold, one salvaged seed pod germinates. She tends it, finally among people who answer when she speaks. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging, hope rooted in sacrifice.
